assessment: The observations establish unmet suitable-time requests, access conflicts and variable administrative load, but do not establish whether usable capacity is insufficient. Unrecorded acceptable windows, equipment needs and total rehearsal needs prevent assessment of the 90% target. Both proposed mechanisms remain hypotheses.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: replacing inherited repeating allocations with a needs-based schedule could improve access within existing capacity. Protect the two performances, allocate each requesting group its guaranteed weekly 60 minutes, then allocate additional time against stated needs and acceptable windows.
openings.delta: Allocate room-time from explicitly recorded needs rather than inherited 90-minute reservations; treat piano eligibility as a requirement to establish, not infer from blank records.
openings.prediction: If inherited allocations rather than unavoidable demand concentration explain exclusion, a candidate schedule will meet more stated needs than the incumbent schedule using the same rooms and hours. If no feasible allocation exists after recording alternatives, this mechanism will not establish the target.
openings.probe: Use the available short contact conversations, by telephone or in person, to record weekly duration needs, acceptable windows, equipment and minimum usable session length. Compare incumbent and candidate allocations against that same demand list, explicitly checking weekly guarantees and performance locks before adopting changes.
assumptions: Contacts can specify needs and acceptable alternatives.
A guaranteed 60-minute allocation is not counted as fully meeting a longer rehearsal need.
Feasibility within all fixed constraints remains unproven.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: one authoritative booking ledger with numbered reservations, explicit supersession of changes and room/time readback could reduce conflicting expectations and reconciliation work.
openings.delta: Make telephone and desk requests update one record before confirmation; mark the second calendar with its update time and confirm bookings from the authoritative record.
openings.prediction: Conflicts caused by inconsistent records or unacknowledged changes should decline; conflicts despite matching current confirmations would implicate another cause. Administrative time may increase if recording overhead exceeds saved reconciliation.
openings.probe: During the eight weeks, record conflict causes, confirmation identifiers and total weekly administration minutes. Test the fewer-than-two-conflicts and two-hours-average targets while continuing to measure stated needs met; preserve existing guarantees and performance bookings.
assumptions: The volunteer and desk can consistently consult the authoritative ledger.
Participants can receive confirmations verbally without digital accounts.
Record inconsistency explains only some observed conflicts.
